claims.statement: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation generally applies from 12 August 2026, covers all packaging, and introduces manufacturing, composition, recyclability, reuse, labelling, and waste-management requirements.
Poland's BDO system includes structured reporting for products, packaging, and waste, creating an existing downstream reporting event that packaging master data can feed.

Hypothesis: distributors and co-packers have a structural reason to embed the rules at specification and quote time because they control the material data and can convert compliance into higher-retention product sales.

contrary_evidence: Micro-enterprises face lighter rules, which may reduce urgency in the easiest-to-reach segment.
The Commission continues to issue exemptions and clarifications, so deterministic advice can age quickly.

economics.acquisition_route: Enter through one packaging material category and one distributor, then expose an API to its brand customers and 3PL partners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 20 distributor or 3PL licences plus 50000 paid SKUs could reach 5 million PLN ARR in years 5-7; at 30% EBITDA, 6x EBITDA, and 75% ownership, founder equity could be roughly 8.1 million PLN
economics.founder_time: 15-22 hours weekly initially; target 8-10 hours weekly after partner-led data capture and contracted regulatory updates
economics.gross_margin_basis: A versioned rules and data API can support 82-92% gross margin; expert rule maintenance is the major fixed cost
economics.payback: Target under 9 months for the channel partner via reduced specification rework and differentiated packaging sales
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 30-120 PLN per active SKU annually, 2-8 PLN per validation event, and 40000-160000 PLN annual distributor licence
economics.retention_or_repeat: SKUs persist for years, market expansion and rule changes trigger revalidation, and quantity exports recur each reporting period

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Supplier declarations, material taxonomies, jurisdiction mappings, and accepted SKU histories improve rule coverage and switching costs
fingerprint.customer: Packaging distributors, co-packers, 3PLs, e-commerce brands, and FMCG manufacturers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Built into distributor quoting, co-packer onboarding, 3PL merchant setup, and packaging procurement tools
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Embedded packaging rules, evidence, and EPR master-data API with per-SKU and partner pricing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Channel partner pays per validated SKU or annual licence when a compliance-ready quote or master-data record is issued
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A packaging SKU is specified, quoted, ordered, or introduced into a new national market

founder_fit: Strong FMCG adjacency, EU/Polish data workflow fit, and reseller economics. The founder's current employer creates conflict-of-interest and confidentiality boundaries: validation must use public rules, synthetic examples, and independent partners, never employer data or time outside policy.
risks: Incorrect rules can lead to unusable packaging inventory or reporting errors.
Enterprise packaging software vendors may add similar modules.
Maintaining many national rule variants could overwhelm a small team unless rollout is narrow.

structure.control_point: The packaging specification approval inside a distributor quote or co-packer onboarding flow
structure.critical_dependency: Continuously maintained jurisdiction rules and trustworthy supplier composition declarations

thesis: Create a packaging-SKU rules and evidence engine embedded in packaging distributors, co-packers, and fulfilment providers. At quote or onboarding it would capture composition and weights, flag market-specific design and labelling issues, preserve supplier declarations, and produce EPR-ready quantity exports; the channel partner monetises compliance-ready packaging rather than sending each brand to a separate consultant.
title: PackRule Embed
uncertainties: National EPR data and fee rules remain fragmented even with harmonised packaging design rules.
Packaging distributors may regard compliance logic as free sales support rather than paid software.
Reliable composition and recycled-content declarations from upstream suppliers may be missing.
